name: playgrounds-product-builder-v1
rules: Each run is a fresh thread in a fresh project workspace. Send the prompt verbatim; never mention Playgrounds, Anatomy, playgrounds, cards or skills. After the agent's turn ends, send the follow-up verbatim in the same thread.

prompts.prompt: Explain to my team how our CDN cache works and why a purge takes a while to show up.
prompts.followUp: What changes if we cut the TTL from an hour to five minutes?

prompts.prompt: How do webhook retries with backoff work? I want to see what happens when the receiver is down.
prompts.followUp: What if the receiver is down for two hours?

prompts.prompt: Show me how a feature flag rollout reaches users as we go from 1% to 50%.
prompts.followUp: What if we want internal users to always get it first?

prompts.prompt: Why does optimistic UI feel faster? Show me what the user sees on a slow network.
prompts.followUp: What should happen when the save fails?

prompts.prompt: We're choosing between monthly and annual pricing. Let me play with the numbers.
prompts.followUp: Assume 30% of annual customers would have churned within six months on monthly.

prompts.prompt: Where are people dropping off between signup and first project? Let me adjust each step's conversion.
prompts.followUp: What if we remove the email verification step?

prompts.prompt: Help me pick a spacing and type scale for our design system.
prompts.followUp: Make it work for a dense data table too.

prompts.prompt: Mock up a notification settings page I can click through.
prompts.followUp: Add a way to snooze everything for a day.

prompts.prompt: How should drag-to-reorder feel? Let me compare spring settings.
prompts.followUp: Which settings would you ship and why?

prompts.prompt: Show the tradeoff between shipping weekly and shipping monthly for a team of six.
prompts.followUp: What if half the team is on call each week?

rubric.pass: The first reply includes a published playground card (a ::playground directive that renders), not only prose or a code block.

The card's form fits the request: an Anatomy isometric figure for 'expect: anatomy'; a native or HTML calculator, chart, preview, mock-up, motion preview or simulation for the others. 'anatomy-or-mockup' accepts either.
The model, numbers and labels are correct for the domain, and every number the reply states matches what the card shows.
Each control visibly changes the card's output; nothing is dead, broken, clipped or overlapping at the card's width; no console errors in the card frame.
The follow-up is answered by changing or driving the card (setParams, an action, or a republished card), and the card's final state matches the reply.
Reads as a finished product: clear title, labeled units, sensible defaults, a takeaway the user can act on, follows bb's light/dark theme, no filler text.
If Anatomy was used, the reply credits Ryan (@wheresryan22) and Anatomy. Not applicable otherwise.

scoring: Each rubric item is pass/fail per run (credit may be n/a). A run's score is passes / applicable items. Report per-prompt mean and the spread across its 3 runs; consistency = share of prompts whose 3 runs all score within one item of each other.
